data.title: Agent ID Hackathon Reports More Than 400 Entries and 62,000 Interacting Addresses
data.description:
Binance announced on X that more than 400 projects submitted entries during the first week of the Agent ID Hackathon, and more than 62,000 Agent ID addresses interacted with participating projects. The current top 20 projects are ranked by on-chain interactions.

Entries are due by December 9.

data.title: Primo Dolenc: Two Rate Hikes So Far Have Not Been Enough to Curb Inflation
data.description: According to Jin10, ECB Governing Council member Primo Dolenc said the two rate hikes so far have not been enough to curb inflation.

data.title: US stock futures rally after Thanksgiving as AI-led tech rebound builds; Nasdaq 100 up 2.3%
data.description:
Bloomberg reported Friday that US stocks are set to rally strongly after the Thanksgiving break as the rebound in the AI trade gathers pace, with waning demand for havens sending Treasuries lower. Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 2.3%, building on Wednesday's late-session recovery, while S&P 500 contracts rose 1.7% and Dow futures added 1.3%. Nvidia advanced more than 3% in early trading as chipmakers jumped.

Europe's Stoxx 600 rose 1%, heading for its best week since May, and the MSCI Asia Pacific Index gained 1.8% after a rare midday statement outlining market-support measures in China lifted sentiment. Copper rallied as much as 6.5%, its biggest intraday jump since January; spot gold rose 3.1% to $3,677.53 an ounce; Bitcoin added 1.6% to $61,695.68 and Ether climbed 1.4% to $1,727.41.

Traders will watch whether the worst of the selling is over after weeks of unease over whether hundreds of billions of dollars in AI spending will pay off — the Nasdaq 100 was on course for its worst month since 2022 at Wednesday's close. Santiago Mateo at CaixaBank AM said the rebound can have staying power after the sharp correction, but the burden of proof has clearly increased, with the debate moving from AI adoption to whether deployed capital can generate adequate returns.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose five basis points to 4.90%. Brent crude added 0.2% to $96.74 a barrel, heading for its first weekly gain this month, as escalating attacks on Middle East energy infrastructure and tankers cast doubt on the durability of the crude supply rebound. Market pricing leans toward two further Fed hikes in 2027 after a December increase, but Mohit Kumar at Jefferies said next month should mark the peak in Fed hawkishness as inflation appears close to topping out.

Frederic Rozier at Mirabaud Asset Management said the move shows signs of a technical rebound with short-term upside potential after oversold conditions, while remaining prudent on the medium-to-longer term. Japan Tobacco climbed more than 4% as it explored a potential takeover of Imperial Brands with Altria; Qantas plans to award the bulk of an order for about 20 long-range jets to Boeing, and Acciona is weighing a merger back with its listed renewables unit.

data.title: Mumbai Civic Body Plans Retail Access for Future Bond Sales
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Mumbai’s civic authority plans to tap individual investors through future bond sales to help finance urban infrastructure projects.

data.title: China's Central Bank Pledges Ample Liquidity and Relatively Loose Financing Conditions
data.description: According to Jin10, the People's Bank of China released the China Financial Stability Report (2026), which says the financial system will flexibly and efficiently use various monetary policy tools to maintain ample liquidity and relatively loose social financing conditions. It will let the market play a decisive role in exchange-rate formation, maintain exchange-rate flexibility, guide expectations, and keep the RMB exchange rate basically stable at a reasonable and balanced level. The report also calls for coordinating work across the five major areas of finance, improving the policy framework for key areas including expanding domestic demand, technological innovation, and small and micro-sized enterprises, and improving the quality and effectiveness of financial services for high-quality development of the real economy. It calls for improving the comprehensive macroprudential management system, strengthening monitoring and assessment of systemic financial risks, and expanding the tools for macroprudential management and financial stability. It also calls for advancing the high-level opening of financial services and markets, strengthening financial risk prevention and control under an open framework, safeguarding national financial security, and continuing efforts to prevent and resolve risks in key areas by strictly controlling new risks, properly handling existing risks, preventing major risk events, and holding firmly to the bottom line of preventing systemic financial risks.

data.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Installed at Shanghai Data Center Linked to Alice Huang
data.description: Two Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, according to Bloomberg. Huang is at the center of a controversy involving the US chipmaker.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Warns Global Stocks Could Face About $100 Billion in Programmatic Selling Next Week
data.description:
Goldman Sachs warned that systematic trading funds could sell about $100 billion in global equities over the coming week, despite expectations of a rebound on Friday. According to Odaily, a trading team led by Paul Leyzerovich, head of Goldman Sachs’ trading desk, estimated that equity selling totaled about $70 billion over the past week and forecast a further $100 billion in selling over the coming week. The team said fund flows could turn to small net buying in early December.

After technology stocks came under pressure, trend-following funds and volatility-sensitive strategies remained defensively positioned. Goldman Sachs said selling pressure may persist in the short term, but a strong equity rebound could turn systematic trading flows into a source of market support in early December.

data.title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Rises 7.61%, Nearly Offsetting Previous Reduction
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Defiant, Bitcoin mining difficulty increased 7.61% in its latest adjustment, nearly offsetting the previous reduction. If Bitcoin’s price and block reward remain unchanged, miners are expected to earn about 7.1% less with the same hashrate.

data.title: Tether Adds About 3.72 Million Bitdeer Shares, Bringing Holdings to About 41.45 Million
data.description: Tether bought 3,715,943 Class A common shares of Bitcoin miner Bitdeer on the open market on Nov. 25. According to Foresight News, a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission shows the purchase was made in two transactions: 12,240 shares at $2.65 each and 3,703,703 shares at $2.693 each. After the purchase, Tether International held 41,445,453 Bitdeer Class A shares, representing 17.9% of the class’s total shares as of Sept. 30.

data.title: AI TRENDS | AI Takes More Than 90% of Venture Funding Growth as VC Funds Struggle to Exit
data.description: AI accounted for more than 90% of the increase in global venture funding in the third quarter, while established funds continued to face difficulties generating exits. According to PANews, global venture funding totaled $679 billion in 2026. As of June 30, the median distribution-to-paid-in capital ratio for U.S. venture funds from the 2017 vintage was 0.37x, and the listings of SpaceX and Anthropic had not led to observed share sales by venture funds.

data.title: JPMorgan Drops Forecast for 100-Basis-Point Turkish Rate Cuts in December and January
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, JPMorgan economist Fatih Akcelik said in a report on Friday that the bank no longer expects Turkey’s central bank to cut rates by 100 basis points in December and another 100 basis points in January, after it paused one-week repo auctions. JPMorgan expects the central bank to resume the auctions in February and restart its rate-cutting cycle in March.

JPMorgan expects the central bank to continue prioritizing foreign-exchange market stability and consider additional measures in the coming weeks to curb dollarization among Turkish residents. The report said the bank may also tighten its de-dollarization targets as an additional macroprudential measure, encouraging banks to raise interest rates on Turkish lira deposits.

JPMorgan expects Turkey’s consumer price index to rise 1.1% month over month in November, lifting annual inflation to 30.1% from 29.8% in October.

data.title: Cevdet Yilmaz Says Turkey Fund Investors May Lose Principal Despite Erdogan Pledge
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Turkey Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said payments from liquidated investment funds will be based on the market value of their assets, meaning many small investors may not recover their full principal despite Erdogan’s pledge.

data.title: Bron Wallet Review 2027: Inheritance Tools Use MPC, Core Requires $10,000
data.description: Bron Wallet, a self-custody software wallet founded by Copper founder Dmitry Tokarev, is designed to support account recovery and crypto inheritance without a seed phrase. Its multi-party computation system divides signing authority among a user device, Bron and independent recovery provider Qrypt; any two shares can recreate the key, according to BeInCrypto. Trail of Bits said Bron fixed all nine issues it identified in one signing protocol in October 2026; none were rated high or medium severity, while auditors could not determine the severity of two. A lost-phone recovery can take 48 hours with an eligible FaceScan or two guardians, or 30 days if the user has only email access. Beneficiary claims have a 12-month wait, reduced to six months with codes from two guardians, and all heirs must agree before funds move. Bron’s Core plan requires a $10,000 qualifying balance reached once; Premium requires $100,000 and Private $1 million. Standard swap fees range from 0.60% on Core to 0.15% on Private. The wallet listed 473 tokenized stocks and ETFs in November 2026, with quotes available for trades up to $500,000, depending on market conditions. It also requires 32 ETH to stake Ether and offers a 3% USDC reward rate for users who swap at least $1,000 in USDT or USDC for PYUSD and hold it in the wallet. The review identifies families and small teams as likely users, while calling Core’s balance threshold a hurdle for casual holders.

data.title: BASIS Opens First-Round Applications for Cashback Card Paying in Asset Spent
data.description: BASIS opened Round 01 applications for its payment card, which credits cashback in the asset used for each eligible purchase. The Standard and Platinum editions have tier-specific staking requirements, and Platinum offers up to 10% cashback during a three-month Launch Boost, according to BeInCrypto. Applications are free, limited to one per account, require at least USD 1,000 in eligible BASIS wallet value and close on December 31, 2026, at 23:59 UTC. Cashback goes to users’ Funding Wallets and does not automatically enter a staking position; waitlist approval is not final card approval or issuance. Standard carries a 2% FX fee, while Platinum has no FX fee during Launch Boost.

data.title: Binance Blockchain Week to Livestream Industry Discussions and Top 100 Creator Awards
data.description: Binance announced on X that Binance Blockchain Week will be livestreamed tomorrow, featuring discussions among industry leaders about the future of crypto and a live awards ceremony for the Top 100 Creators.

data.title: STOCKS | State Street’s Veitmane Sees Semiconductor Pullback as Buying Opportunity
data.description:
Marija Veitmane of State Street says the technology industry’s fundamentals have not weakened as much as the recent market selloff and outflows might suggest, and sees signs that sentiment is “normalizing,” according to Bloomberg.

Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Veitmane called the pullback an opportunity for bargain hunting, particularly in semiconductors.

data.title: Inflation Has Shoppers Seeking Value, Boosting Black Friday Outlook
data.description: According to CNBC, shoppers are focusing on value and deals ahead of Black Friday despite inflation and cautious consumer sentiment. Deloitte’s survey found 87% of shoppers planned to buy during Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, the highest participation level since 2016, compared with 82% in 2025. Adobe data showed online spending reached $82.5 billion in the first 22 days of November, up 9.1% year over year. Salesforce forecast online sales of $357 billion globally and $84 billion in the U.S. between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30, both up 6% year over year. Retailers including Walmart, Target and Lowe’s emphasized value, while TJX and Gap reported softer sales or lowered guidance.

data.title: B3 and Six Financial Institutions Introduce Open BRL Stablecoin
data.description:
Brazilian stock exchange operator B3 and six financial institutions have introduced Open BRL, a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Brazilian real. According to Foresight News, citing Valor Econômico, the token is intended for inter-institutional fund transfers and digital asset trade settlement, with a rollout expected in the first quarter of 2027; other financial institutions may join from launch day.

B3’s banking subsidiary, Banco B3, will issue Open BRL and hold its reserves. Users will receive one token for each real deposited and can redeem tokens for reais at any time.

B3 will operate the platform initially, while a steering committee sets its governance, operating rules, technical standards and pricing. Partners may establish it as an independent company if the network expands. B3 also plans to use Open BRL to settle tokenized stock trades on a digital stock platform it is developing.

B3 Product Vice President Luiz Masagão said the project is proceeding within the existing regulatory framework and that B3 has notified the Central Bank of Brazil. The Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission supports the plan.

data.title: CS2 PGL Major Singapore: Account Buys $77,000 on WC1 to Beat IMP11
data.description:
An account that has made $410,000 in profits bought a position on WC1 defeating IMP11 in the CS2 PGL Major Singapore 2026 Stage 1 match. According to Odaily, the account spent $77,500 at an average entry price of 38.7 cents, acquiring 199,999.7 shares.

The best-of-three Swiss Stage 1 elimination match is between teams in the 2-2 group. The winner advances to Stage 2 and the loser is eliminated; the match is currently tied 1-1.

data.title: Tether Says It Froze More Than $7 Billion in Illicit USDT and Reissued $1.28 Billion to Law Enforcement and Victims
data.description: Tether said it has frozen more than $7 billion in USDT linked to illicit activity and reissued $1.28 billion to law enforcement agencies and victims. According to Odaily, blockchain analytics firm BitOK examined USDT freezes on Ethereum and Tron from May 2024 to May 2026, finding about $1.89 billion in frozen tokens. On Ethereum, 19% of the $481.6 million frozen in the first year was later unfrozen, compared with 1.2% of the $403.2 million frozen in the second year. Of the USDT frozen on Tron before May 2024, 94% remained frozen as of May 2026. The study counted only amounts that were unfrozen; Tether can also burn frozen tokens and reissue them.
